records.question: What documents should I prepare?
records.answer: Use the personalised Home Affairs checklist for your passport country, provider and circumstances, then ImmiAccount requests. Typical evidence includes identity/passport, CoE, GS responses and supporting study/employment records, and applicable English, financial, OSHC, health and character evidence. Family applications may need relationship, birth, schooling and parental-consent or custody documents. This is not a universal mandatory list.

records.question: Do I need a Confirmation of Enrolment?
records.answer: Generally, provide a CoE for intended courses when applying. Special categories have alternative evidence.

records.question: Do I need English language evidence?
records.answer: English test evidence or a documented exemption may be required. Check the applicable tests, scores and exemptions before applying.

records.question: What financial evidence is needed?
records.answer: Financial evidence covers travel, living, tuition and relevant dependant schooling costs. Verify current amounts separately.

records.question: Do I need OSHC?
records.answer: OSHC generally covers you and accompanying dependants throughout your stay; some nationality-based exceptions apply.

records.question: What should I prepare for accompanying family?
records.answer: Eligible partners and dependent children may apply as secondary applicants. Check relationship and birth evidence, schooling, parental consent or custody, finances and OSHC for accompanying family. Eligibility depends on the family circumstances; inclusion is not automatic.

records.question: Are there extra requirements for students under 18?
records.answer: Students under 18 need evidence of appropriate accommodation and welfare arrangements.

records.question: What identity evidence should I prepare?
records.answer: Provide a passport copy and other specified identity documents where available.

records.question: Should my documents be translated?
records.answer: Documents not in English need English translations as well as copies of the originals. Translator identification requirements depend on location.

sources.title: Home Affairs — Applying for a student visa

records.question: Can I leave important documents until later?
records.answer: Prepare required evidence before lodging and follow Home Affairs submission guidance. Check your personalised ImmiAccount requests.

sources.title: Home Affairs — Applying for a student visa

records.question: What is the Genuine Student requirement?
records.answer: Study must be the main purpose of the application. Explain your circumstances, course/provider choice and future benefit with supporting evidence. Possible future permanent residence intentions do not by themselves count against GS.

records.question: What changed from GTE to GS?
records.answer: Applications lodged from 23 March 2024 are assessed under Genuine Student; applications lodged earlier are assessed under Genuine Temporary Entrant.
records.previousRule: Genuine Temporary Entrant applied to applications lodged before 23 March 2024.
records.currentRule: Genuine Student applies to applications lodged on or after 23 March 2024.

records.question: Does GS affect someone who already studies in Australia?
records.answer: GS applies to applications lodged from 23 March 2024. Holding a valid visa does not itself trigger a fresh GS application. A further application is assessed under the applicable current rules; previous Australian study, progress, provider changes and study gaps may matter.

records.question: Should I attach a separate GS statement?
records.answer: Home Affairs prefers responses in the application form. Answers are in English, limited to 150 words each, with supporting evidence.

records.question: How much can an international student work?
records.answer: The general Subclass 500 limit remains 48 hours per fortnight while the course is in session. A fortnight starts Monday and lasts 14 days. Check VEVO and the exceptions; no general increase above 48 hours was established in this review. The date of this review is not a new work-rights commencement date.

sources.title: Home Affairs — Work restrictions and VEVO

records.question: Do international students have workplace protections?
records.answer: International students have workplace protections, including minimum employment entitlements. The Fair Work Ombudsman can assist with workplace issues.

sources.title: Department of Education — International students at work

records.question: Could changing my course affect my visa?
records.answer: Changes to study can affect a visa. Check the applicable requirements and notification process before making a change.

sources.title: Home Affairs — Changes in your situation

records.question: Should I report a new passport or changed details?
records.answer: Home Affairs asks visa holders to notify relevant changes, including passport, contact, family, work or study circumstances.

sources.title: Home Affairs — Changes in your situation

records.question: Who can give immigration assistance?
records.answer: Use a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or an eligible exempt person. Confirm the adviser’s authority to provide immigration assistance.

records.question: Does every student receive the same visa duration?
records.answer: Length of stay depends on the intended course and relevant insurance and welfare coverage. Check your granted expiry date and the applicable guidance.

records.question: Are research students and compulsory placements exempt from the work cap?
records.answer: Condition 8105 includes exceptions for a commenced research masters or doctorate and qualifying compulsory work registered as part of the course. A coursework masters does not give the primary student the research exception. Check the course and granted conditions.

records.question: Can I work before the course starts or during breaks?
records.answer: Generally work cannot start before the course begins. There is a prior-visa work-permission exception. The primary student term-time cap does not apply during scheduled course breaks; verify whether the course is actually in session, including relevant exams or other study. Family members have different rules.

sources.title: Home Affairs — Work restrictions and VEVO

records.question: Can my spouse work more than 48 hours?
records.answer: Secondary Student visa holders generally have a 48-hour fortnightly limit, including during course breaks. The masters/doctoral exception for family differs from the primary student research exception and can include coursework masters. Course commencement and prior-visa exceptions matter. Check condition 8104 and VEVO rather than assume identical rights for both partners.

sources.title: Home Affairs — Work restrictions and VEVO

records.question: Can my family join me later?
records.answer: Check that your visa permits subsequent entrants and that family members were previously declared. Later family applications still need to meet their own requirements. If family circumstances changed after the original application, obtain case-specific guidance rather than assume the general declaration rule decides the outcome.

sources.title: Home Affairs — Bringing a partner or family

records.question: Does my family need to satisfy GS?
records.answer: Student visa applicants must meet GS or the GS dependent criterion as applicable. Family inclusion does not remove the dependent assessment.

records.question: What changed from MD111 to MD115?
records.answer: For offshore Student visa processing, the Home Affairs page distinguishes MD111 before 14 November 2025 and MD115 from that date. MD115 has three priority levels rather than two. Priority concerns processing order, not approval, a visa cap or guaranteed completion time.

sources.title: Home Affairs — Student visa processing priorities

records.previousRule: MD111 processing framework before 14 November 2025: two priority levels.
records.currentRule: MD115 for offshore applications lodged from 14 November 2025: three priority levels.
records.newStudentImpact: Check offshore lodgement date and the relevant provider/category priority.
records.currentStudentImpact: An already-granted visa is not reassessed by a processing-priority change. Pending and further applications need their own lodgement context.

records.question: Does a child change subsequent-entrant processing priority?
records.answer: Under the published MD115 categories, subsequent-entrant applications including a minor are Priority 1; those without a minor are Priority 2. This affects processing order only, not family eligibility or a promised decision date. The distinction is also listed under MD111, so it must not be described as newly introduced by MD115.
